uncertain_sources: The classroom eigenvector discussion is mathematically loose; the chapter preserves the question while stating that Lorentzian signature and the causal cone do not select a preferred timelike observer.
A timelike geodesic locally maximizes proper time, while the sign-reversed action minus m times tau is locally minimized.
The lecture uses a latitude-like angular coordinate, producing cos squared theta rather than the more common sin squared theta.
The live radial Hamiltonian algebra contains false starts; the chapter uses the convention-consistent conserved-energy expression implied by the displayed Lagrangian.
The Hawking-radiation remark is retained only as a quantum-field aside and is not presented as a result of the classical radial-ray calculation.
The Schwarzschild solution is consistently identified as an exterior vacuum solution, so the formal Earth Schwarzschild radius is not treated as an Earth horizon.
